Overview of retrieval in RAG: RAG addresses a model's lack of up-to-date knowledge by sourcing and incorporating knowledge from external databases. Retrieval is one of three core components, alongside generation and augmentation.","citationIds":["c1"]},{"text":"II. Pre-retrieval process: Indexing optimization aims to improve the quality of indexed content through strategies such as enhancing data granularity, optimizing index structures, adding metadata, alignment optimization, and mixed retrieval.","citationIds":["c2"]},{"text":"Query optimization makes the user's question clearer and more suitable for retrieval, using methods like query rewriting, transformation, and expansion.","citationIds":["c2"]},{"text":"III. Retrieval strategies: Hybrid retrieval integrates keyword, semantic, and vector searches. Sub-queries and HyDE aim to improve relevance through embedding similarities between generated answers and real documents.","citationIds":["c3"]},{"text":"IV. Post-retrieval process: Retrieved context must be integrated with the query, mainly through reranking chunks and context compression. Reranking moves the most relevant content to the edges of the prompt.","citationIds":["c2"]},{"text":"V. Iterative and adaptive retrieval: Retrieval need not be sequential. Examples include the iterative Retrieve-Read-Retrieve-Read flow of ITER-RETGEN, and adaptive methods such as FLARE and Self-RAG that evaluate whether retrieval is necessary.","citationIds":["c3"]},{"text":"VI. Example retrieval system (HippoRAG): Offline indexing uses an LLM to extract noun phrase nodes and relation edges via OpenIE, and a retrieval encoder to add synonymy edges when cosine similarity exceeds a threshold. At retrieval, the output PPR node probability is aggregated over indexed passages to rank them.","citationIds":["c4"]},{"text":"VII. Evaluation and baselines: Common baselines include BM25, Contriever, GTR, and ColBERTv2, plus LLM-augmented methods (Propositionizer, RAPTOR) and multi-step retrieval (IRCoT). Retrieval is reported with recall@2 and recall@5.","citationIds":["c5"]}],"citations":[{"id":"c1","chunkId":"396a0fadeb4cd40f_c_589bc4e8cae01e02","docId":"396a0fadeb4cd40f","docTitle":"2312.10997_Retrieval_Augmented_Generation_for_Large_Language_Models_A_Survey","page":2,"quote":"RAG bridges this information gap by sourcing and incorporating knowledge from external databases."},{"id":"c2","chunkId":"396a0fadeb4cd40f_c_ff1814eb2a0b5efa","docId":"396a0fadeb4cd40f","docTitle":"2312.10997_Retrieval_Augmented_Generation_for_Large_Language_Models_A_Survey","page":4,"quote":"This involves strategies: enhancing data granularity, optimizing index structures, adding metadata, alignment optimization, and mixed retrieval."},{"id":"c3","chunkId":"396a0fadeb4cd40f_c_445a807c7c2b8b50","docId":"396a0fadeb4cd40f","docTitle":"2312.10997_Retrieval_Augmented_Generation_for_Large_Language_Models_A_Survey","page":5,"quote":"Hybrid retrieval strategies integrate keyword, semantic, and vector searches to cater to diverse queries."},{"id":"c4","chunkId":"14671c78fc7de99d_c_e2ab10a48622bc45","docId":"14671c78fc7de99d","docTitle":"2405.14831_HippoRAG_Neurobiologically_Inspired_Long_Term_Memory_for_Large_Languag","page":4,"quote":"we first use L to extract a set of noun phrase nodes N and relation edges E from each passage in P via OpenIE."},{"id":"c5","chunkId":"14671c78fc7de99d_c_1561f63effe8dae8","docId":"14671c78fc7de99d","docTitle":"2405.14831_HippoRAG_Neurobiologically_Inspired_Long_Term_Memory_for_Large_Languag","page":5,"quote":"We compare against several strong and widely used retrieval methods: BM25 [69], Contriever [35], GTR [53] and ColBERTv2 [70]."}]}}}
